Subject: Post-call recap: Reranker integration & eval questions

Thanks again for the excellent call today, Sarah — appreciate the time and the clarity on Acme's ranking goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope an integration POC: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: Replace heuristic scoring in search with a learned reranker to improve relevance for payments dispute queries (primary) and merchant lookup (secondary).
- Current infra: embeddings computed offline (OpenSearch ingestion) + a simple BM25 + rule-based score; client latency SLO for search page is 200ms.
- Success metrics mentioned: CTR on first result, NDCG improvement, and a reduction in manual escalations.

Open/Action items (please confirm owners):
1) Technical integration approach (Redwood reranker endpoint vs local model). Owner: Redwood (Dev) + Acme Eng.
2) Auth & SDK setup: will Acme want token-based server-server calls or a VPC/private endpoint? Owner: Nikhil + Acme infra.
3) Routing/top_k: default top_k to re-rank? We discussed re-ranking top 50 then returning top 5. Need confirm.
4) Eval plan: sample size, metrics (MAP@k, NDCG@k, Recall@k), and baseline exports. Owner: Acme to share sample queries and labels; Redwood to propose default configurations.
5) Timeline: POC data exchange and a 2-week eval window.

I've attached a short eval spec template (reranker_eval_spec.xlsx) and a sample CSV template for queries — please fill / confirm back. Dev, can you weigh in on 1 & 2 below?

Next steps I suggest:
- Acme to share a sample of ~2k labeled queries (or at least top 500 with relevance buckets) and a representative logs export by EOD Fri 2026-02-27.
- Redwood to propose a POC architecture doc and an endpoint test harness by Tue 2026-03-03.
- Schedule a 30-min technical follow-up next week to finalize auth and routing.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming a few things and answering your open items: 

- We'll aim to provide ~2k labeled examples but can definitely get 500 high-quality labels by Friday. Labels are relevance buckets (0/1/2) rather than graded relevance for now.
- Latency: the 200ms SLO is at the user-facing page render. We are fine with doing an offline rerank step that reindexes scores if it helps with latency, but would prefer an online score for highest-value queries.
- Auth: server-to-server token is preferred (we manage secrets in HashiCorp Vault). A private VPC endpoint is an option if needed for PII-sensitive exports.
- Top_k: re-rank top 100 from current ranker and return top 5 seems reasonable. We are flexible if you have a better default to test.

Couple of clarifying questions for your engineers: 
1) How does Redwood handle embeddings/ID mapping for reranking? Do you require us to upload vector store snapshots, or can you call our embeddings endpoint?
2) For evaluation, we typically compute NDCG@5 and Recall@5. Is MAP@k something Redwood can compute in the out-of-box eval harness?

Thanks — Sarah

Thanks, Sarah — good context. A few technical notes and options from our side to help you decide the integration pattern: 

Option A — Redwood-hosted reranker endpoint (fastest POC):
- You send query + candidate doc IDs + precomputed embeddings (optional). Redwood will call our ranking model to score candidates and return top_k sorted IDs.
- Auth: bearer token (server-to-server). We support token rotation hooks for Vault.
- Pros: no infra changes on Acme, we handle model variants, instrumentation, and eval harness.
- Cons: network roundtrip; we'll need to agree on candidate set size to meet your latency SLO. Re-rank top 100 is achievable in ~80-150ms for our mid-tier models depending on doc length.

Option B — Client-side scoring (embedding + local model):
- You run a lightweight reranker or quantized model in your infra; Redwood can provide pretrained checkpoints and kernel suggestions.
- Pros: lowest latency, full data control.
- Cons: requires infra + ops.

Embedding/id mapping: we accept either: (1) vector snapshots you upload to a temporary S3/GCS location (we ingest and run eval), or (2) streaming evaluation where you POST candidate vectors with each query. For a POC, snapshot (1) is easiest — send a CSV mapping doc_id -> vector (or provide location).

Eval metrics: We support NDCG@k, Recall@k, MAP@k, and precision@k in our eval harness. We also compute position-weighted CTR lift if you have click logs. Default in our POC is NDCG@5 and Recall@5 + MAP@5; we can run NDCG@10/MAP@10 as a follow-up.

Suggested POC plan:
- Acme: provide 500 labeled query-doc pairs + candidate set snapshots (CSV) by 2026-02-27.
- Redwood: run baseline rerank (our mid-tier reranker) and return NDCG@5, Recall@5, MAP@5 within 5 business days.
- Joint sync: 30-min to review results and tune top_k.

I'll prepare a short architecture diagram (endpoint request/response payload) and a sample SDK snippet (Python + Node) demonstrating auth and the ranking call. Marissa — can you confirm if we should include the SDK snippet in the same doc for the customer?

— Dev

Dev — this is super helpful, thanks. A few quick answers: 
- We'll do the snapshot upload to S3. I'll share a signed URL for a 2k sample by Friday.
- We're happy with Redwood running a mid-tier reranker for the POC. Please include both NDCG@5 and MAP@5 in the baseline. If you can surface per-query delta from baseline (our current heuristic) that would be ideal.
- We use position-weighted CTR internally as well — would like that metric exported if possible.

Attached a CSV sample (acme_sample_queries.csv) with query IDs and relevance buckets for the 500-item sample. Also linking a short doc with notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-re-ranker-eval

If you could provide a recommended default for top_k to re-rank for the POC, that helps. Based on our scale and your latency numbers, top_k=100 -> return 5 seems like the right starting point.

Best — Sarah
